comment.text: ACVR1B R485 is represented as a recurrently mutated residue in Cancer Hotspots v1. Source observations include Colorectal carcinoma; Gastric adenocarcinoma. Statistical enrichment supports review as a candidate somatic hotspot; it does not establish the functional effect, pathogenicity, or treatment sensitivity of every alteration at this position. This site is present only in the historical V1 material in this collection.

applicability_notes: Confirm the exact allele and reference transcript: source protein numbering is not a validated clinical HGVS assertion.
Tumor counts describe source cohorts and may overlap between releases and sheets; they must not be added together.
An observed synonymous or stop allele is retained for source fidelity and is not automatically classified as oncogenic.
FDA references are separate gene-level evidence until the exact biomarker, tumor, setting, and current label have been checked.

report_comment.text: Somatic alterations affecting ACVR1B residue R485 have been observed in colorectal carcinoma and gastric adenocarcinoma. The functional and clinical significance depend on the specific alteration and tumor type.

comment.text: ACVR1B R485* is an allele annotation observed in Cancer Hotspots v1 at the R485 hotspot or indel region. This documents recurrence in the source cohorts; allele-specific function, tumor-specific significance, reference-sequence mapping, and clinical actionability require independent review.

report_comment.text: The ACVR1B R485* alteration has been observed in colorectal carcinoma and gastric adenocarcinoma. Its functional and clinical significance require allele- and tumor-specific assessment.
